title: SQL Day 2 Coding Arena — Ranking & Aggregation

questions.scenario: The manager wants a clean list of product categories.
The manager wants the largest orders first.
questions.request: Return order ID, customer, and sales sorted highest to lowest.

questions.scenario: Leadership only wants the five largest orders.
questions.request: Return the top five orders by sales.
Return category and total sales by category.

questions.scenario: Leadership needs a region-level revenue view.
questions.request: Return region and total sales, highest revenue first.
questions.validation: GROUP BY region and ORDER BY total_sales DESC.

questions.scenario: The team wants its highest-value customers.
questions.request: Return customer and total sales, highest total first.

questions.scenario: Only high-revenue categories should appear in the executive report.
questions.request: Return categories whose total sales exceed 100000.

questions.scenario: The VP wants only strong regions.
questions.request: Return regions with total sales above 75000, ordered from highest to lowest.
questions.validation: HAVING threshold and descending aggregate order.

questions.scenario: The CFO wants the most commercially important customers.
questions.request: Return the top ten customers by total sales with customer name and total sales.
questions.validation: GROUP BY customer_name; SUM(sales); ORDER BY total_sales DESC; LIMIT 10.

questions.scenario: Leadership wants a ranked category performance table containing only categories above a defined threshold.
questions.request: Return category, total sales, and average profit for categories with total sales above 50000, ordered by total sales descending.
questions.validation: Correct grouping, HAVING threshold, aggregate measures, and ordering.
